summary: What worked: capacity. The baseline model was undersized for the 300s budget, and on top of the halved batch (TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**18, already measured by peers at ~0.9877) both more depth (d512 L8 0.9877 -> L10 0.985230) and more width (d768 L8 = 0.981817, the cell's best) pay off. My best own run is 0.984380 (dim 768, depth 8, batch 2**18, DB=128, GQA n_kv_head 6->3). What did not: head_dim 128->64 (1.003546), depth 12 (0.985159, flat vs depth 10), stacking depth and width (depth 10 x dim 640 = 0.986355, worse than either alone and a clean replication of a peer's 0.986247), width past the optimum (dim 896 = 1.043352), and GQA (0.984380 vs 0.981817 for the same shape with full MHA). I also measured that the 'DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 + grad_accum 2 to fit VRAM' trick costs ~0.05 bpb at fixed tokens-per-step, across three runs. Next I would hold dim 768 / depth 8 / batch 2**18 / DB=128 with full MHA and spend runs on what the shape scan cannot reach: MLP expansion ratio 4x vs 3x at that width (the shape knob I never got to), re-tuning matrix_lr for the 1.5x wider model, and the window pattern, since the 768 optimum is sharp enough that per-token cost matters more than raw parameters.
